extracted.intended_audience: news publishers, journalists, newsroom product teams, and researchers interested in how Facebook ranks news posts
extracted.subtask_description: A concise description of the algorithmic signals Meta uses to surface news posts in the Facebook News Feed; intended to guide publishers and others about what content and source attributes are prioritized. Covers top-level signals (who posted it, post type, quality, engagement predictions, trust, timeliness, originality) and explicit implicit newsworthiness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Posted It
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency of past engagement with the source; "Friends/family first"; Trusted page (authentic publisher); Subscribed/followed source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals prioritize content from sources a user has engaged with in the past, content from friends and family, pages verified as authentic publishers, and pages/users the individual has explicitly followed or subscribed to. Publisher reputation and prior interaction history influence ranking weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Type
rubrics_metrics.description: User's past engagement with that content type (video, link, photo, status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The algorithm models a user's format preferences and boosts content types the user typically interacts with (for example, video vs. link vs. photo vs. status). Format affinity influences which items are shown higher in the feed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and Format
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertical orientation (mobile-first); Clean visuals; Authentic content (anti-misinformation signals); Original sources prioritized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual and format features that signal higher production or mobile-friendliness (e.g., vertical videos, clear imagery) are favored. Content flagged as inauthentic or misinformation is deprioritized. Posts that point to or originate from original sources are given priority over lower-quality/aggregated formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement Predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Likelihood user will: comment, like, share, save, click; Likelihood of meaningful interaction (comments > likes); Watch time / view duration on video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ranking uses predictive models estimating specific engagement actions; meaningful interactions (such as comments) are weighted more heavily than passive reactions. For video, watch time and view duration are key signals. These predicted engagement metrics strongly influence which posts are surfaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust Signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether content is from publishers users have rated as broadly trusted; Authenticity verification; Penalty for engagement bait, sensationalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher trust ratings collected from users and other verification signals contribute to a source trust score. Content that appears to manipulate engagement (engagement bait) or uses sensationalist tactics is penalized. Authentication (e.g., publisher verification) increases ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Timey Posts" — currently popular content; News value boost for breaking stories; Decay function on older posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recency and current popularity matter: posts about unfolding, breaking stories receive a news-value boost. Popularity spikes ('timey posts') can be elevated, while older content experiences decay in ranking over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original News Boost (specific to news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta has a "prioritizing original news" model that boosts: First-source reporting; Original investigation; Penalty for aggregation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content identified as original reporting or the first publication of a story receives an explicit boost. Aggregated or rehashed coverage is penalized relative to original sources. Models aim to surface the earliest and most original coverage of news events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement prediction (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond raw counts, the implicit signal is a predicted probability of engagement; in practice comment-type interactions are treated as more meaningful and weighted higher than likes/reactions when determining newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source trust score (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An aggregate measure of how broadly trusted a publisher is (based on user ratings and verification) that influences ranking. Higher trust scores increase the likelihood content from that source is surfaced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals that detect inauthentic behavior (bots, spam) or manipulated content reduce ranking. Authenticity checks and anti-misinformation signals are integrated into quality assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual quality (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posts with clean, high-quality visuals and mobile-friendly format (e.g., vertical orientation) are favored. Poor visual presentation can decrease engagement predictions and thus ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How new the content is; newer content generally ranks higher, and older posts have a decay function applied that reduces visibility over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original reporting and unique investigations are prioritized; derivative or aggregated content is penalized. Originality is a key component of the dedicated 'original news' boost.

rubrics_metrics.name: User affinity (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A user's demonstrated interest in a source or topic (past engagement patterns, follows/subscriptions) increases the likelihood similar content will be shown; personal affinity signals are a primary personalization factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format friendliness (implicit)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content that matches device and platform preferences (e.g., mobile-first vertical videos) and formats that users typically engage with are more likely to be surfaced. Format friendliness interacts with post type and engagement prediction signals.
